origin.rerun: grep -n 'if "deferred" in low' src/runtime/order_monitor.py; grep -n 'elif _res == "deferred"' -A6 src/runtime/order_monitor.py | grep -n _attempt_naked_autoprotect  # both present = the sweep still re-arms straight after ANY deferred breach exit, including a working extended-hours limit

what: [money-path] The equity naked sweep's breach exit fights its own close in EXTENDED hours (#14585 re-review note; root-caused from code 2026-09-30). Path: _check_broker_naked_equity_positions → pre-flight 'exit_breached' → _exit_alpaca_row → _send_close_to_exchange → AlpacaClient.close → session 'extended' → _close_extended_hours. That cancels the symbol's orders and POSTs a DAY extended-hours LIMIT sized to the row, and on non-fill returns retCode 2 'extended-hours limit close working — not yet filled, exit deferred'. _exit_alpaca_row matches the word 'deferred' and returns 'deferred'. The sweep's `_res == 'deferred'` branch then calls _attempt_naked_autoprotect AT ONCE. AlpacaClient.place_protective → _scoped_rearm_cancel counts that working close-limit as the position's OWN leg (a protective type, reducing side, qty == row qty), CANCELS it and posts a GTC OCO. Net effect: the exit order the sweep just placed is undone. It is replaced by a stop that Alpaca does not trigger outside regular hours, and the monitor's next strategy close tick cancels that stop again. That is REARM-VS-CLOSE-FIGHT on a path #14585 did not touch: the sweep never calls mark_active_close. Fix direction: distinguish 'working limit' (reached the broker; leave it and do not re-arm) from 'nothing sent' (closed session; re-arm is right) in _exit_alpaca_row's return, e.g. key on 'bracket left armed', with a test. Tier-2 order-path, to be a HELD PR. Also a nit: .github/pr-landing/alpaca-close-wedge-rearm.json hold_text item (3) still says any session-deferred re-probe is held; after the F1 fix only a nothing-sent defer is.
